# New TunePad cell
# These variables store the MIDI numbers for drum sounds.
# Kick is the bass drum, snare is the backbeat,
# and hat is the closed hi-hat.
kick = 36
snare = 38
hat = 42

# This function plays one drum sound.
# The note number selects the sound.
# The duration controls how long the note is played.
def drumHit(note, duration):
    playNote(note, beats=duration)

# This function creates the main kick and snare rhythm.
# The kick starts the bar and the snare adds a backbeat.
# All note lengths and rests add up to four beats.
def mainDrums():
    drumHit(kick, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    drumHit(snare, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    drumHit(kick, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    drumHit(snare, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)

# This function creates a slightly different drum pattern.
# The extra kick makes the rhythm less repetitive.
def drumVariation():
    drumHit(kick, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    drumHit(snare, 0.5)
    drumHit(kick, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    drumHit(kick, 0.5)
    drumHit(snare, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)

# This function plays a hi-hat rhythm.
# The loop plays eight short notes in one bar.
def hiHat():
    for i in range(8):
        drumHit(hat, 0.5)

# This function creates the full drum section.
# Every fourth bar uses a different drum rhythm.
def playDrums():
    for bar in range(8):
        if bar % 4 == 3:
            drumVariation()
        else:
            mainDrums()

# Play the main drum rhythm.
playDrums()

# New TunePad cell
# This function plays a chord using a list of MIDI notes.
# "notes" contains the pitches and "duration" controls the length.
def playChord(notes, duration):
    playNote(notes, beats=duration)

# This function creates one bar of piano rhythm.
# It plays a long chord, pauses, and then plays two shorter chords.
# The total length of this pattern is four beats.
def pianoPattern(chord):
    playChord(chord, 1.5)
    rest(0.5)
    playChord(chord, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    playChord(chord, 1)

# These lists contain the MIDI notes for four R&B chords.
# Each list is stored in a variable so it can be reused.
am9 = [57, 60, 64, 67, 71]
dm9 = [50, 53, 57, 60, 64]
g13 = [55, 59, 62, 65, 64]
cmaj9 = [48, 52, 55, 59, 62]

# This list stores the order of the chords.
# The for loop goes through the list one chord at a time.
progression = [am9, dm9, g13, cmaj9]

# This function plays all four chords in order.
# Each chord uses the same rhythmic pattern.
def playPiano():
    for chord in progression:
        pianoPattern(chord)

# This loop repeats the four-chord progression twice.
# It creates eight bars of piano music.
for i in range(2):
    playPiano()

# New TunePad cell
# This function plays one bass note.
# "pitch" controls the note and "duration" controls its length.
def bassNote(pitch, duration):
    playNote(pitch, beats=duration)

# This function creates the first bass rhythm.
# It uses the root note and a higher note.
# rest() creates silence between the sounds.
def smoothBass(root):
    bassNote(root, 1.5)
    rest(0.5)
    bassNote(root + 7, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    bassNote(root + 12, 1)

# This function creates a second bass rhythm.
# It uses shorter notes to add some movement.
def bassVariation(root):
    bassNote(root, 1)
    rest(0.5)
    bassNote(root + 7, 0.5)
    bassNote(root + 12, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    bassNote(root + 7, 1)

# This list stores the root MIDI notes of the four chords.
# The lower notes create the deep bass sound.
bassRoots = [33, 38, 31, 36]

# This function creates one four-bar bass section.
# range(4) makes the loop run four times.
def playBass():
    for i in range(4):
        root = bassRoots[i]

# The % operator checks whether i is even or odd
# Even bars use smoothBass and odd bars use bassVariation.
        if i % 2 == 0:
            smoothBass(root)
        else:
            bassVariation(root)

# Repeat the bass section twice to match the piano.
for i in range(2):
    playBass()

# This function plays one melody note.
# The pitch is a MIDI number and beats controls its duration.
def melodyNote(pitch, duration):
    playNote(pitch, beats=duration)

# This function creates the first melodic phrase.
# The notes move upward and then return to a lower pitch.
def phraseA():
    melodyNote(69, 1)
    rest(0.5)
    melodyNote(72, 0.5)
    melodyNote(76, 1)
    melodyNote(72, 1)

# This function creates a softer second phrase.
# The longer final note gives the melody more space.
def phraseB():
    melodyNote(74, 0.5)
    melodyNote(72, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    melodyNote(69, 1)
    melodyNote(65, 1.5)

# This function creates a higher melodic phrase.
# Short notes create movement before the final long note.
def phraseC():
    melodyNote(71, 0.5)
    melodyNote(74, 0.5)
    melodyNote(77, 1)
    rest(0.5)
    melodyNote(74, 1.5)

# This function creates the ending of the melody.
# It returns to C and E to create a gentle feeling.
def phraseD():
    melodyNote(76, 1)
    melodyNote(74, 0.5)
    melodyNote(72, 0.5)
    rest(0.5)
    melodyNote(71, 0.5)
    melodyNote(72, 1)

# This function combines the four melodic phrases.
# Each phrase lasts four beats.
def playMelody():
    phraseA()
    phraseB()
    phraseC()
    phraseD()

# Repeat the melody twice to create eight bars.
for i in range(2):
    playMelody()
